subject: Re: Discovery recap — Trial scope, model stack recommendation and owners
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novamed.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Trial scope, model stack recommendation and owners

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the claims intake flow and the localization requirements for ES/DE/FR. Short recap + proposed next steps and POC outline below so we’re all aligned.

Recap (2 min):
- Goal: reduce TTR on claims triage and surface correct policy clauses in replies; support live agents with suggested responses in Spanish and German.
- Volume profile: ~120 reqs/hr during peak, median input length 220 tokens, spikes to 2–3k tokens for large claims.
- Success metrics you emphasized: 1) accuracy of policy extraction (F1 target >= 0.85 on test prompts), 2) agent adoption (suggested reply accepted >= 45%), 3) 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for streaming snippets.

Proposed 4-week Trial (owner/next steps):
- Week 0 (prep): SSO + test dataset handoff (owner: NovaMed IT), security intake & SLA (owner: Dylan).
- Week 1: baseline measurement using sample prompt set; integration with a single agent UI endpoint (owner: Marissa).
- Week 2: focused tuning (prompt engineering + small system prompt variants); run automated acceptance tests.
- Week 3: multilingual evaluation and live shadow testing; collect adoption metrics.
- Week 4: acceptance run & handoff to ops; decision checkpoint.

Model stack recommendation (initial + fallback):
- Primary (recommended for accuracy & longer-context handling): Llama 2 70B Chat — quantized 4-bit runtime to hit latency targets while preserving instruction-following. It handles long context better for your 2–3k token spikes with Redwood’s KV caching turned on.
- Fallback (cost-sensitive / burst mode): Mistral 7B Instruct — faster spin-up and lower token cost for high-throughput windows.
- Multilingual support: run the primary with a light translation/normalization preprocessing for German/Spanish. If we see regressions, fail over to Falcon-40B-Instruct-lite (proposal) or a specialized EU fine-tuned 13B polyglot model we can onboard for the trial.

Data & compliance notes:
- For EU residency: we can pin the trial to our Frankfurt region; logs can be TLA encrypted and retained per your policy. I’ll kick off security intake and attach the security FAQ.

Attachments: mutual action plan, sample prompt set, security FAQ (attached).

Request / ask: Please confirm (A) budgeted trial window (we proposed 4 weeks starting next Monday), (B) IT contact for SSO & data residency, and (C) whether the agent UI can expose streaming tokens in the shadow test.

Next steps after confirmation: we’ll provision a dedicated trial environment and share a short integration checklist.

Thanks —
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Trial scope, model stack recommendation and owners

Hi Dylan,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Timing — we are aiming for a mid-May start but need internal sign-off from Procurement (budget) and Security. Procurement needs an estimate of expected token spend (ballpark) for the 4-week run.
2) Residency — Frankfurt is required for PHI-adjacent metadata; please confirm logs will remain in-region.
3) Languages — Spanish + German are must-haves. If you propose an interim translation step, can you include expected latency overhead?
4) Acceptance criteria — your F1 >=0.85 target looks reasonable. Can Marissa share a short test plan (how we compute F1 / acceptance)?

Security contact: copying Tom Reilly (SecOps) — Tom, can you share the standard questionnaire items you need?

If we can get the Mutual Action Plan and a token-spend estimate today we’ll expedite Procurement.

Thanks,
Alicia

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Trial scope, model stack recommendation and owners

Thanks Alicia — answers below and a couple of small asks.

1) Token spend estimate (ballpark): for the trial profile you gave (120 reqs/hr peak, median 220 tokens, with 10% large at 2k tokens) we estimate ~1.1M tokens over 4 weeks on the primary model. Cost depends on runtime/quantization; preliminary estimate attached in the Mutual Action Plan (sheet: cost-estimate). Ben, can you confirm if that aligns with Redwood’s trial credit policy?

2) Residency: confirmed — we can pin the environment to Frankfurt and configure log retention/rotation per your policy. All logs will be encrypted at rest; we will not export raw customer data outside the region.

3) Latency overhead for translation step: lightweight translation proxy (batch translate 1–2 sentences) adds ~50–120ms median depending on segment size. For large documents we recommend translating only the agent-facing extractive snippets to keep 95th percentile latency in target. We’ll instrument this in Week 2 shadow testing.

4) Acceptance/Test plan (short):
- Golden set: you provide 200 labeled claim samples in EN/ES/DE with expected policy tags.
- Metric calc: policy extraction F1 (macro) and suggested-reply acceptance % (UI metric). We’ll run 3 replicated sweeps with seed prompts; acceptance requires F1 >= 0.85 and suggested-reply acceptance >=45% on the EN baseline and no more than 10% delta in ES/DE.

Ownership & contacts (proposal):
- Redwood trial lead: Dylan Brooks (provisioning, infra, security intake)
- Redwood success manager: Marissa Cole (integration, evaluation, test-run owner)
- NovaMed trial lead: Alicia Gomez (business owner)
- NovaMed SecOps: Tom Reilly (security questionnaire and sign-off)

Attachments included: the Mutual Action Plan has the cost tab and a short checklist; sample_prompt_set.csv contains 30 initial prompts we used for baseline runs; Security FAQ has our standard answers for common questions.

Small asks: please attach the 200 labeled golden set when you can, and confirm whether Procurement needs a formal quote or the mutual action plan is sufficient for internal approvals.

I’ll queue up provisioning once Procurement confirms.

Best,
Dylan

Hi Alicia / team,

Looping in with the abbreviated test run plan we mentioned — keeping it lean so Procurement can sign-off quickly: 

POC acceptance checklist (short):
- Data handoff: 200 labeled claims (EN/ES/DE) delivered to our secure S3 in Frankfurt (owner: NovaMed).
- Baseline run: Redwood runs three replicates against Llama 2 70B Chat + KV cache enabled.
- Multilingual check: same runs with translation proxy + native run on fallback model (Mistral 7B) for comparison.
- Performance: 95th pct latency <=450ms on streaming snippets, memory footprint within dedicated pool limits.
- Quality: F1 >=0.85 on policy extraction; suggested-reply acceptance >=45% on EN with ES/DE <=10% delta.

Deliverables at trial close: short evaluation report (metrics + sample failure cases), configuration recipe for production (recommended quantization and batch settings), and rollout checklist for dedicated capacity.

Marissa (cc) will orchestrate the baseline runs and share a one-page results template you can forward to Procurement.

If that all looks good, Alicia, can you authorize start on Monday May 15 and drop the golden set to the Drive link in the Mutual Action Plan?

Thanks —
Marissa
